name: Marietta Works
summary: Two walled squares of 50 and 27 acres, flat-topped mounds and a graded way down to the Muskingum, with the Conus mound and its ring to the south. The town of Marietta was laid out over it in 1788; the Conus mound survives in Mound Cemetery.
notes: The squares and the graded way are gone under streets. What the LiDAR still shows: the Conus mound and its ring ditch in Mound Cemetery, and two raised blocks where the flat-topped mounds Quadranaou and Capitolium stood (the county library sits on Capitolium).
Too little wall survives for the automatic search, so this plate is placed by three hand-picked points: the Conus mound and the two platform mounds.
Charles Whittlesey surveyed it in 1837, with the town's streets drawn in; the same streets are still there.

plate.label: Plate XXVI
